messages:
Caroline M: Quick sync — product wants to consolidate our weird 490-series client codes into a smaller, predictable surface. goal: consistent HTTP semantics for clients + clear console/SDK guidance for action (retry vs fix auth vs quota). looking for input on mapping, telemetry, and console wording.
Drew (oncall): +1 on the consolidation. main risk is customers who have logic branching on exact numeric codes. we need a migration signal and fallback plan. deprecation window?
Ben S: I agree. proposal sketch:
- preserve semantics but map to canonical http codes (e.g., 490x -> 400/401/403/429 depending on cause)
- emit a header so clients can detect old-vs-new: `x-redwood-original-code: 4903`
- add telemetry for both canonical and original code so we can measure impacted customers
Alice K: rough mapping example (we can iterate):
```
4901 -> 400 (bad request)
4902 -> 401 (invalid creds)
4903 -> 429 (rate/quota)
4904 -> 403 (policy disallowed)
```
also propose `x-redwood-hint: "retry-after:60;action=backoff"` for actionable hints.
Eva R: console UX ideas:
- surface a small badge on request traces: "Client error (non-fatal)"
- when expanded show: canonical code, original code (if present), human-friendly suggestion (fix request / check auth / contact support)
- include a one-click copy of suggested retry header/sample SDK snippet
Ben S: for rollout/cadence: keep old numeric behavior for 90 days while emitting header + console flag. After 90d start returning canonical codes but still include `x-redwood-original-code` for another 180d. Final removal 270d after announcement unless major breakage.
Drew (oncall): SDK behavior: log a warning when deprecated code seen; optionally surface DeprecationWarning API so apps can trap it. We should coordinate minor SDK patch that doesn't break existing error classes.
Caroline M: copy needed in-console and in-API docs. sample console text: "This request failed with a client error. Suggested action: check request payload and auth. If you rely on numeric codes, see migration notes." need i18n-ready short + long strings.
Ben S: concrete console phrasing suggestion (short): "Client error — check request or auth. See migration guide (opens)."
Ben S: (long): "We are standardizing several legacy codes to canonical HTTP statuses to improve portability. We will include an `x-redwood-original-code` header during the migration period so existing client logic can detect the legacy code. See: docs link"
Alice K: telemetry: add metric `client_error.original_code_seen` with tag `original_code` and `mapped_code`. also increment counter for `client_error.migration_impact` when we see SDKs from older versions.
Caroline M: what about retry semantics and idempotency hints? we should avoid encouraging blind retries. prefer explicit `retry-after` hints or `action=do-not-retry` in `x-redwood-hint`.
Eva R: Console drilldown should recommend exact action: e.g., "Action: Do not retry — quota exceeded. Visit quota page or request increase" or "Action: Retry with backoff — transient rate limit". show links to relevant console pages.
DocsBot: I'll draft the migration guide and i18n strings. will add code snippets for Go/JS/Python SDKs and a sample `curl`.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/rdw-code-migration-2026 (tracked)
Drew (oncall): ops checklist: add alert when `client_error.original_code_seen` spikes > 0.5% of requests during rollout. enable canary in eu-west first.
Caroline M: decision-levels: agree on mapping + header + 90/180/270 day timeline. action items: 1) Ben — finalize mapping table + sample console copy; 2) Alice — telemetry metrics and docs for metrics; 3) DocsBot — migration page; 4) Drew — SDK warning plan + canary rollout. I'll consolidate into RFC and schedule stakeholder review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Ben S: taking mapping + copy, will post PR with examples by EOD.
Alice K: will add metrics + dashboards mock tomorrow AM.
Eva R: I'll mock console UX and put screenshots into the RFC draft.
Caroline M: thanks all — if you see customer pain while this is in flight, ping me directly. We'll leave the `x-redwood-original-code` on by default during rollout.
